findings.problem: fs::read_to_string file I/O is fused with parse logic in load_metrics; the parse boundary is crossed by raw path: String into domain Record with no separation of shell I/O from pure parsing.
findings.failure_mode: I/O errors abort the request instead of returning typed errors, and pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested or reused without touching the filesystem.
findings.fix: Extract a pure parse_metrics(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> function. Have load_metrics call it after fs::read_to_string, mapping I/O errors with map_err into a typed error taxonomy (FileRead, Parse, Invalid).

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap on Result from file I/O is a panic surface in production code.
findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission errors, or unreadable paths cause a process panic instead of returning a typed FileRead error to the caller.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::FileRead(e))? or fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| ParseError::Io(e))?.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on Result from numeric parse is a panic surface in production code.
findings.failure_mode: Non-numeric value in the second CSV field causes a process panic instead of returning a typed ParseError::Invalid to the caller.
findings.fix: Replace with parts[1].parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)? using split_once, or parse with u32 then u16::try_from().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)?.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked index access on a split result with no bounds check. The code collects split parts into a Vec then indexes by position, and if the line does not contain a comma or has only one field, the index access panics.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV input (missing comma, empty line, or single-field line) triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic at runtime instead of returning a typed error.
findings.fix: Replace line.split(',').collect() with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? and bind as let (name_str, value_str) = ...; to avoid index access entirely.

findings.problem: value: u16 field combined with .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy as cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values exceeding 65535 without any domain validation or error.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in the range 65536-4294967295 silently wraps to a wrong u16 value, corrupting data with no error returned to the caller, violating the no-lossy-casts absolute law.
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16: .parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid)?, or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)?

findings.problem: Vec<String> is allocated via collect() into a Vec with no try_reserve and no domain cap validation. The final collect() on line 22 also lacks try_reserve.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded input can trigger uncontrolled heap allocation with no graceful error handling, violating the bounded resources and allocation discipline laws.
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap/max rows first, create Vec::new(), call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?, enforce max before each push, and return typed errors for TooMany or Allocation.

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses Actions (fs::read_to_string file I/O), Data (Record struct construction), and Calculations (parsing, splitting, string trimming) into a single function. The parse boundary is not respected.
findings.failure_mode: Pure parsing logic cannot be tested or reasoned about independently of file system state. Hidden side effects in a function that appears to be data loading make reasoning about program state impossible.
findings.fix: Extract parse_metrics(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> using split_once, return Result from load_metrics wrapping I/O and parse errors in a typed LoadError enum, keep Record as a pure data type.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — stdout logging is fused inside the data-loading function, which should be pure calculation/logic.
findings.failure_mode: Side-effectful logging inside what appears to be a data transformation function breaks determinism, makes pure testing impossible, and couples the core logic to a specific I/O channel.
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing logic entirely. If metrics/logging are needed, have the shell wrapper handle logging after parse_metrics returns.

findings.problem: No try_reserve call and no bounded allocation pattern. The function does not validate a domain cap or use try_reserve before collecting results, violating the bounded resource law.
findings.failure_mode: An attacker or malformed input file can trigger arbitrary heap allocation, leading to DoS via memory exhaustion with no graceful error recovery.
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap first: let mut records = Vec::new(); records.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?; then enforce max_items before each Record push, returning TooMany or Allocation errors.

findings.fix: Run with allocation profiler (e.g., criterion with measurement_type=WallTime and alloc_count, or dhat-rust) to capture allocation profiles, then eliminate per-line Vec allocations via split_once.
